text:
Priya (CS): Quick capture from today's Acme onboarding call — high-level asks and friction points. They mentioned: 1) per-route billing toggle (want to test cost vs quality), 2) more explicit retry/error visibility in Console, 3) embeddings drift when customers use long docs, and 4) request for a small 'self-serve' tuning guide. Thinking a short 'feature bounty' list we can groom and triage for Q2. TL;DR: two high-impact asks (billing toggle + retry visibility), two medium (embeddings/explainability + guide).

Evan - PM: this is gold, thanks. Can you drop the raw notes + any logs? I'll slot the top two into next planning if impact/effort looks reasonable. Also, can we get a concrete customer example for embeddings drift?

Priya (CS): Adding the doc: https://drive.redwood/example/acme-call-notes — raw transcript + compact summary. Embedded a short example payload they sent for embeddings:
```
{"doc_id":"A-77","text":"... ~12k chars with many headers and PDFs pasted in ..."}
```
They said similarity results degenerated after ~8k tokens.

Lena (Support): saw a similar ticket from BetaHealth last month — filed as INC-2891. Customers see near-duplicates and low recall when document length goes up. I can paste the anonymized sample.

Tom (Eng): for embeddings drift: is this more about chunking strategy or the model encoding? If we can reproduce with the sample we can test chunk sizes + overlap.

Marcos (PS): from the field, the billing-toggle ask is common among larger accounts — they want to run pilots where heavy embedding routes are isolated to a paid/high-cost tier. Could be gated behind a per-route flag in Console. Low effort if we expose existing route config, medium effort if it needs backend gating + billing instrumentation.

Priya (CS): csbot logged a signal: "customer_signal: Acme - feature_ask:feature_bounty/3180301234" — link to ticket: https://redwood.atlassian/CS-4321 

csbot: New customer signal recorded: CS-4321 (Acme). Priority: candidate.

Evan - PM: proposal: convert to a tiny groom session tomorrow. Quick checklist: 1) validate reproducibility (Tom), 2) mock Console toggle UI (Design), 3) estimate cost/instrumentation (Finance), 4) draft self-serve tuning guide (Docs). Who can own steps 1 & 4?

Tom (Eng): I can take reproducibility. Will try to run a few experiments with the sample tomorrow. If I find it's chunking, we can recommend overlap + semantic chunk boundaries as an interim.

Priya (CS): I'll draft the customer-facing guide (short how-to + recommended settings) and share a Google doc by EOD tomorrow.

Lena (Support): I'll attach the anonymized BetaHealth sample to the ticket and link any related logs. Quick note: support currently sees ~7 such tickets in last 6 weeks flagged as "embedding quality" — may help prioritization.

Evan - PM: cool. For prioritization, I'm leaning: 1) billing toggle (customer revenue + pilotability) 2) retry/visibility (SLOs + churn risk) 3) embeddings drift (engineering investigation) 4) tuning guide (low effort, high value). Sound right?

Marcos (PS): agree w/ ordering. Also recommend we offer Acme a brief paid pilot for the billing toggle — can de-risk and cover engineering time. I'll draft a short pilot proposal.

Priya (CS): note to team — customer asked for timelines. Can we give a safe estimate for the pilot/proof-of-concept?

Tom (Eng): won't know until repro. But if it's chunking, we can give a 2-week spike + 1-week patch for interim guidance. If deeper model issues, it's longer.

Evan - PM: OK, action items: Tom -> reproduce (owner). Priya -> guide draft + customer comms. Marcos -> pilot proposal. Lena -> attach tickets + samples. I'll add a 1-pt groom and a possible 2-3 wk spike in next sprint if Tom confirms.

Priya (CS): I'll send Acme a note: "we heard you, opening pilot discussion + short guide" and link CS-4321. Draft below: 
"Hi Alex — thanks again. We're opening a pilot to help isolate per-route cost/quality and will share a short tuning guide this week. We'll follow up with estimated timelines after a quick engineering spike. — Priya"

Evan - PM: +1. One more ask: can Support add a short severity tag to each related ticket ("revenue-risk" vs "ux-annoyance")? That will help triage.

Lena (Support): will do. I'll mark Acme + BetaHealth as revenue-risk for now.

csbot: Label update: CS-4321 tagged with [revenue-risk].

Tom (Eng): I'll post quick notes in the ticket when I start experiments.

Priya (CS): thanks team. Will follow up tomorrow with the guide draft and link to the groom. If anyone thinks we should deprioritize the 'guide' in favor of building the toggle, flag now.

Evan - PM: not deprioritizing both; guide is quick and protects customers until we build toggle. Let's keep momentum. :rocket:

Marcos (PS): noted — I can demo pilot ask in customer call next week if we have a sketch.

Priya (CS): closing loop here — attaching next steps to CS-4321 and scheduling a 15-min groom for tomorrow 10am PT.

Lena (Support): added related tickets + samples.

Evan - PM: thanks all.
